lens: Lens 2 — codegree (C2), overlap of projections and alternating conditional expectations (C3), applied to the hub-diagonal pairing P = (TA_b∘T)(TC_b)^T of F1/F2 and to the layer-to-layer map of the chain. Net 0, Φ-gated cocycle T = W_9 D(Φ_8)…W_{l'+1} (the chain's own cocycle), sources l' = 8, 6, 3 (ages 1, 3, 6), legs A_b = D_Φ S_b, C_b = A_b D_{w2} with S_b the birth covariance minus its top eigenpair (sec_transport Prop. 'Coherent, cross and bulk parts'). Scripts/logs: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-thehonesttorus-github-io/9523ef6a-ff73-5ab2-8be3-275df2b5fcc6/scratchpad/wf/lens2/{hub_overlap,hub_onesided,alt_expect,crosscov_floor}.py and .log.

claims.claim: Codegree form and C2 double count of the bulk hub pairing. With U = TA_b∘T and Z = TC_b, P_ik = Σ_r U_ir Z_kr = ⟨U_i, Z_k⟩_hub is a signed weighted codegree (for 0/1 incidences it is |N(i)∩N(k)|), and ‖P‖_F² = ⟨U^TU, Z^TZ⟩_F = Σ_r |u_r|²|z_r|² + Σ_{r≠r'} ⟨u_r,u_r'⟩⟨z_r,z_r'⟩ (degree part + codegree part; this is C2's Σ_z|S∩N(z)|² = Σ_{u,v∈S}|N(u)∩N(v)| with hubs as vertices). Likewise the W_l-ensemble variance of the cubic pairing is a hub double count: for i≠k, E P_ik² = (2/n)³[Σ_{rr'} G^A_{rr'}G^M_{rr'}G^C_{rr'} + Σ_{rr'} H_{rr'}H_{r'r}G^C_{rr'} + Σ_{rr'} d_r d_{r'} G^C_{rr'}], G^X = X^TX for X = MA_b, M, MC_b (T = W_l M), H = (MA_b)^T M, d = diag H. Measured on net 0: the codegree (r≠r') share of ‖P‖_F² is −0.2%, +0.6%, +0.4% at ages 1, 3, 6 (iid Gaussian T of the same norm: −0.7%, +1.4%, +0.7%); the Wick formula matches 12 resamples of W_9 to 0.2–0.6% (ratios 1.002, 0.994, 1.004) and its r≠r' share is −0.09%, +0.14%, +0.83%. The Gram of the n rank-one hub pieces u_r z_r^T has rms off-diagonal / mean diagonal = 0.006 and net off-diagonal sum ±0.5% of the diagonal.
claims.status: PROVED (identities; one line each, Wick for the variance) and CHECKED (hub_overlap.py (I1)–(I3), hub_onesided.py; exact to float for (I1),(I2))
claims.argument: (I1) is the definition of a matrix product. (I2): ‖UZ^T‖_F² = tr(Z U^T U Z^T) = Σ_{rr'}(U^TU)_{rr'}(Z^TZ)_{rr'}. (I3): P_ik = Σ_{abc} W_ia W_ib W_kc Q_abc with Q_abc = Σ_r (MA_b)_ar M_br (MC_b)_cr; for i≠k rows i,k of W are independent N(0,2/n), E[W_ia W_ib W_ia' W_ib'] gives the three pairings (aa')(bb'), (ab')(ba'), (ab)(a'b'); contracting Q with itself over the readout indices turns each pairing into a hub Gram pairing. The split r = r' versus r≠r' is then read off. The smallness of the r≠r' share is a sign cancellation (the Hadamard leg's hub-column overlaps are uncorrelated with the Z leg's), not a smallness of the overlaps themselves (see next claim).
claims.consequence_for_system: The pairing sits in the nibble's 'codegree ≪ degree' regime, but with ensemble mean zero (F2). In the nibble that regime makes a count concentrate on its mean; here it makes the NORM self-averaging (std/mean of ‖P‖_F ≈ 1% across W_l resamples, our-data (c)) while the MATRIX is the sum of n mutually Frobenius-orthogonal rank-one hub pieces with random signs: it is all fluctuation and no mean. There is nothing coherent across hubs for a mean (ensemble, coherent, or any low-dimensional summary) to capture, which is the C2 reading of F2/F3 ('bulk pairing is realization-specific; coherent+cross+diagonal recover almost nothing').
claims.test: Repeat hub_overlap.py (I2) for the residual-block bulk terms (2/3)(TR_b∘T)T^T + (1/3)(T∘T)(TR_b)^T from a kprop3 record (R21 from nonlin_step) and with sampled gates: one Hadamard product and two n×n Gram matrices per source-age, ~2 s. If their r≠r' share is also <1%, the incoherence statement covers the entire bulk memory.

claims.claim: Size of the C3 overlap operator for our cocycle. In C3's normalisation (trivial singular pair removed and scaled to 1), the centred overlap of the hub legs is ρ = s_2/s_1: T: 0.995, 0.988, 0.956; U = TA_b∘T: 0.985, 0.863, 0.688; Z = TC_b: 0.892, 0.883, 0.927 at ages 1, 3, 6; the J-part (rank-1 of both legs, i.e. the C3 'replace by the trace state' = the coherent part of F2) carries 0.1% of ‖P‖_F² and rank-k truncation of both legs explains 0.11/0.40/0.65/0.91 of the energy at k = 32/128/256/512 — indistinguishable from an iid Gaussian T (0.11/0.40/0.65/0.91) even at age 6 where T itself has effective rank 35 and 99.5% of its energy in 256 directions. The hub-column correlation matrices Ĝ = D^{-1/2}X^TX D^{-1/2} have ‖Ĝ−I‖ = 3.0, 12.7, 27.3 for T (iid: 3.0), 3.2, 5.8, 11.8 for U, 71, 67, 69 for Z.
claims.status: CHECKED (hub_overlap.py (I4), n = 1024, one network, Φ gates)
claims.argument: C3 says ‖E_PE_Q − J‖ = ρ and ‖(E_PE_Q)^m − J‖ = ρ^{2m−1}: the graph example C = A/d − J has ρ = λ_2/d, and a small ρ (expander) is exactly what makes codegrees ≈ their mean d²/n. For the legs of the pairing the analogue of J is the top singular pair (collective direction) and the analogue of ρ is s_2/s_1. Measured ρ ≈ 0.7–0.99: there is no spectral gap, so no power of the overlap converges to a trace state, and the J-replacement captures 0.1% of the pairing. The flat truncation profile of P equal to the iid one is the Hadamard obstruction of sec_cost: U = TA_b∘T has effective rank 222/147/73 while T has 256/74/35, so the Hadamard leg restores a flat spectrum whatever the cocycle's contraction.
claims.consequence_for_system: 'The overlap operator is not small' is quantitatively: ρ(U) ≥ 0.69, ρ(T) ≥ 0.96 at all ages ≤ 6; the C3 rate ρ^{2m−1} would need ~100 alternations to reach 1e-2 and nothing in the chain alternates. The coherent/collective replacement (rank-1 J) is a 1e-3 approximation of the bulk, consistent with F2's 1.65e-6 → 1.2e-6 when coherent+cross+diagonal are kept. Compression of both legs to the 1e-6 energy precision the sensitivity law requires (F3, F6) needs k ≈ n: at k = 512 the unexplained energy is still 9e-2.
claims.test: Already decisive: the rank-k truncation curve (hub_overlap.py (I4)) versus the 1e-6 target. For a second network, run the same script on W_off1.npy (needs its MC cache for S_b).

claims.claim: Where the n³ sits: one-sided truncations and the birth-rank (hub-profile) form P = Σ_j s_j (U y_j) z_j^T. Writing Z = TC_b = Σ_j s_j z_j y_j^T, the pairing of the hub projections {e_r} with the Z leg's hub profiles y_j gives P exactly; truncating Z alone to rank k explains 0.91/0.96/0.99 (age 1), 0.91/0.97/1.00 (age 3), 0.90/0.98/1.00 (age 6) of ‖P‖_F² at k = 64/128/256 (equal to the Z energy kept), truncating the birth matrix C_b in hub space before transport explains 0.90/0.95/0.98, 0.87/0.93/0.97, 0.75/0.87/0.93, truncating A_b inside the Hadamard 0.84/0.86/0.90, 0.80/0.83/0.88, 0.66/0.73/0.84, and truncating U alone explains only the energy kept (0.25/0.42/0.66). S_b has effective rank 14/20/36 with 87/83/70% of its energy in 64 eigendirections. Per-hub energies |u_r|²|z_r|² have participation ratio 0.37/0.44/0.58 and the top 50% of hubs carry 97/94/84%.
claims.status: CHECKED (hub_onesided.py); the cost arithmetic is PROVED; the use for old sources is CONJECTURE
claims.argument: P = UZ^T has rank ≤ rank Z and P − UZ_k^T = U(Z−Z_k)^T, so a steep Z spectrum (inherited from the birth covariance S_b, not from T) controls P without touching the Hadamard leg; the Hadamard leg U is flat, so truncating it or A_b inside it loses the energy fraction dropped. The required precision is 1 − explained ≈ 1e-6 (slices to 1e-3 by the sensitivity law, F6); the Z truncation reaches 1e-2 at k = 256 at age 1 and 1e-3 at age 6. Cost: with C_b ≈ C_k Y^T, P1 = (UY)(TC_k)^T costs 6kn² against 2n³, i.e. 1.5n³ at k = 256 and 0.75n³ at k = 128, and only the P1 (= P3, our-data identity) product is affected; P2 = (TA_b∘TC_b)T^T and the residual-block terms with T∘T stay dense.
claims.consequence_for_system: The whole n³ memory of a source-age is carried by the Hadamard leg against a dense T^T; the identity leg's partition {e_r} is read against hub profiles that are low-rank only on the non-Hadamard side. The participation ratio 0.4–0.6 is the flat hub-importance profile of F3 (dropping 50% of hubs loses 3–16% of energy, 4–5 orders above tolerance). The birth-rank truncation is not a route at the floor: it saves at most 25–60% of one of three n³ products per source-age (≈3–8% of the chain's bill) for an error of 1e-2–1e-3 in energy on young sources; for sources of age ≥ 4 (worth a factor 6 in MSE, sec_cost) a rank-256 truncation costing ≤0.1% energy might be tolerable, which is the only conjecture here.
claims.test: One kprop3c run (~1 min) with C_b of sources of age ≥ 4 replaced by its rank-256 truncation (A_b untouched), compared with the exact 3.5e-8 and the bill; if the MSE moves by <5% the saving of ~1 n³ per old source-age can be booked, otherwise the birth-rank form is closed.

claims.claim: The layer-to-layer map of the chain is NOT an alternating product of two conditional expectations (onto the previous layer's algebra and the gate algebra), and no overlap operator governs a convergence rate of it.
claims.status: REFUTED (algebraic; nesting checked numerically to 1e-15 in alt_expect.py (B1))
claims.argument: In L²(x), x ~ N(0,I), the algebras are nested: σ(z_{l+1}) ⊂ σ(z_l) because z_{l+1} = W_{l+1} relu(z_l), and the gate algebra G_l = σ(sign z_l) ⊂ σ(z_l). Hence E_{l+1}E_l = E_{l+1}, E_{G_l}E_l = E_{G_l}, and C3's quantity ‖(E_{l+1}E_l)^m − J‖ = ‖E_{l+1} − J‖ = 1 for every m (witness f = standardised z_{l+1,c}: ‖f − W_c·relu(z_l)‖/‖f‖ = 1e-15, so E_l f = f and ‖f − Ef‖ = ‖f‖). The forward map is z_{l+1} = W Π_l z_l where Π_{l,a} is multiplication by the gate projection 1[z_{l,a}>0] — a projection IN the algebra, not a conditional expectation ONTO a subalgebra; the chain's nonlinear step is the nonlinear cumulant map C ↦ E[relu relu^T](C) (arc-cosine kernel), whose Hermite series E[f(z_a)g(z_b)] = ⟨f, T_ρ g⟩ = Σ_k ρ_ab^k f_k g_k/k! contains exactly ONE conditional expectation (E_a g(z_b) = T_ρ g, Mehler) with rate ρ^k in the Hermite degree k, applied once per layer and never iterated; C3's rate ρ^{2m−1} has no m to run over (the exact per-pair statement is E_aE_b|_{σ(z_a)} = T_{ρ²}, i.e. (E_aE_b)^m He_1(z_b) = ρ^{2m−1} He_1(z_a)).
claims.consequence_for_system: No mixing-type (expander, spectral-gap) estimate applies to the chain's depth recursion; the analogue of the C3 rate inside the chain is the Hermite-degree rate ρ_ab^k of the pair moment, where the first-order κ3 transport keeps k ≤ 1 and the O(ρ²) 'ρ-exact gate' is the open 8–10% slice deficit of sec_transport. Nothing in C2/C3 bears on the memory cost (F1) through the layer map.
claims.test: None needed; the statement is algebraic. The only quantitative follow-up is the size of the ρ² gate term, which sec_dictionary already lists.

claims.claim: The centred overlap operator that does exist is the one-step cocycle acting on the covariance, kink-weighted for the gate partitions. For single-neuron algebras σ(z_{l,a}), σ(z_{l+1,c}) (not nested), C3's ρ is the maximal correlation, which equals |ρ_ca| = |Cov(z_c,z_a)|/(σ_cσ_a) for the Gaussian closure; and Cov(z_{l+1}, z_l) = W_{l+1}D(Φ_l)C_l + ½ W_{l+1}D(w2_l)K3_21(l) = T_{l+1←l}C_l + (κ3 slice feed), K3_21[b,a] = κ3(z_b,z_b,z_a). For the two-element gate partitions {p_a,1−p_a}, {q_c,1−q_c} the C3 matrix is 1×1: C_ca = (τ(p_aq_c) − Φ_aΦ_c)/√(Φ_a(1−Φ_a)Φ_c(1−Φ_c)) = ρ_ca φ(α_a)φ(α_c)/√(…) + O(ρ²). Measured (N = 32768, layers 2→3, 6→7, 8→9): Gaussian/Stein part leaves a systematic relative residual 2.9%, 3.8%, 4.1%; adding the κ3 feed the residual is within Monte Carlo noise (cosine of the residuals on two independent halves 0.01, 0.05, 0.07; systematic part ≤ 1.9e-3, 2.2e-3, 2.2e-3). Binned HGR maximal correlation of real pairs: 0.2936/0.2248/0.1467/0.0931/0.0521 against |ρ| = 0.2903/0.2234/0.1404/0.0872/0.0352 and a Gaussian null with the same ρ and N of 0.2946/0.2221/0.1465/0.0865/0.0523 (bias-matched). Gate overlap over 128×128 cross-layer pairs: rms 0.0050/0.0043/0.0042, rms deviation from ρφ_aφ_c 0.00088/0.00063/0.00059 against MC floors 0.00095/0.00061/0.00053, corr 0.985/0.989/0.990. Operator norm of the normalised cross-layer overlap D^{-1/2}(TC_l)D^{-1/2}: 8.4, 24, 34 (s_2/s_1 = 0.97, 0.76, 0.66), median entry 0.035–0.060, max 0.31–0.47.
claims.status: PROVED (Stein's lemma with the Gram–Charlier expansion: Cov(f(z_b),z_a) = Σ_k κ_{k+1}(z_b,…,z_b,z_a)E f^{(k)}(z_b)/k!, with E relu' = Φ, E relu'' = φ/σ = w2; orthant expansion P(z_a>0,z_c>0) = Φ_aΦ_c + ρφ_aφ_c + O(ρ²); maximal correlation of a Gaussian pair = |ρ|) and CHECKED (alt_expect.py (B2),(B3),(B3'), crosscov_floor.py)
claims.argument: Stein's lemma gives the k = 1 term W D(Φ)C_l (the one-step cocycle of F1 applied to the covariance) and the k = 2 term ½ W D(w2) K3_21, which is the transposed-slice feed of Thm transport (eq. cov-transport one order lower); the residual after both is uncorrelated between independent halves, so it is noise at the 2e-3 level, with κ4 contributions below that. The gate-partition overlap is the first-order orthant term, whose weights φ(α_a)φ(α_c) are the kink densities of F6; the first-order formula is exact within noise over 16384 pairs because cross-layer |ρ| is small per entry (median 0.04–0.06) while the operator norm is large through the collective mode (F7).
claims.consequence_for_system: The 'centred overlap operator' of the system, in covariance/cocycle terms, is Cn = D^{-1/2}(T_{l+1←l}C_l + ½W D(w2)K3_21)D^{-1/2}; the gate partitions see D_{w'}(T C_l)D_w, i.e. the same operator weighted by kink densities — the w-weights the chain already carries. Its entries are small and its norm is O(10) because of the collective mode, so any C3-type rate argument would be dominated by the one direction the chain already treats exactly (coherent part); the incoherent bulk (F7: 0.2–5% collective share of the error) is invisible to it. The κ3 slice is literally the first correction to the cross-layer overlap, which is why its memory cannot be dropped without a 3–4% systematic error in Cov(z_{l+1}, z_l).
claims.test: crosscov_floor.py with N = 2^18 and the κ4 (2,2) term added: if the residual falls below 1e-3 with κ4 the Stein series is confirmed to third order; cost ~3 min.

claims.claim: The Euler–Stein merge coefficient a = 1/(p+1) (sec_capacity, F5) is an integrated Gaussian-pair C3 rate: with ρ_τ = (1+τ)^{-1/2} = corr(g, g + √τ ξ) = ‖E_{σ(g)}E_{σ(g+√τξ)} − J‖ (C3 for a jointly Gaussian pair, maximal correlation = |ρ|), a = ∫_0^∞ ½(1+τ)^{-3/2} ρ_τ^p dτ = 1/(p+1), numerically 1.000000, 0.500000, 0.333333, 0.250000 for p = 0,1,2,3.
claims.status: PROVED (calculus: ∫_0^∞ ½(1+τ)^{-(p+3)/2}dτ = 1/(p+1); the identification of (1+τ)^{-1/2} with the C3 norm of the pair (fluctuation g, tilted pre-activation g+√τξ) is the maximal-correlation theorem for Gaussian pairs) and CHECKED (alt_expect.py (B5))
claims.argument: sec_capacity lines 82–96: a = ∫½(1+τ)^{-3/2}g(τ)dτ with g(τ) = (1+τ)^{-1/2} for a defect first order in the births, because the birth strength averages to E φ(α) = (2π(1+τ))^{-1/2} for α ~ N(0,τ); a defect of order p in independent births decays as (1+τ)^{-p/2}. The factor (1+τ)^{-1/2} is the correlation between the un-tilted fluctuation g and the tilted pre-activation g + √τξ, which by C3 (Gaussian case) is exactly ‖E_AE_B − J‖ for their two algebras, and the p-th power is the contraction of a product of p independent such overlaps — the same algebra as the He_p eigenvalue ρ^p of a Mehler operator. The repo already derived a = 1/(p+1); what is new is only the identification, and the remark that the derivation needs the p birth factors to be independent overlaps (the measured 0.256 vs 1/3 is the correction for correlated directions).
claims.consequence_for_system: The only place where a C3-type alternating-expectation rate is literally a constant of the system is the Euler–Stein correction along Eldan's path, not the layer map or the memory. Practical caution for task #13: a short-memory chain's defect is of mixed order in the births (the dropped memory enters at first order, the Gaussian part at zeroth), so g(τ) is a mixture of (1+τ)^{-p/2} and a is not a single 1/(p+1); it must be measured (scripts/defect_profile.py) before the derived constant is used.
claims.test: scripts/defect_profile.py on the window-1/2 chain of task #13 at n = 1024: fit g(τ) at τ = 0.25, 1, 4, 16 to c_1(1+τ)^{-1/2} + c_2(1+τ)^{-1}; the implied a = c_1/2 + c_2/3 against the least-squares a. Cost: 4 chain runs per τ.

verdict: C2 and C3 formalise F2/F3 but add no estimate. The hub pairing is exactly a signed codegree, and its C2 double count is >99% 'degree' (r = r'): the n hub pieces u_r z_r^T are mutually Frobenius-orthogonal with uncorrelated signs (codegree share <1% of the energy and of the W_l-Wick variance, checked on net 0 at ages 1, 3, 6), which is why the pairing's norm self-averages while the matrix is a zero-mean, realization-specific fluctuation that no mean, coherent part, or low-rank summary captures (rank-1 J-part 0.1%, rank-k truncation of both legs identical to an iid matrix: 0.65 at k = 256 against a 1e-6 target). In C3 terms the overlap operator has no spectral gap: s_2/s_1 = 0.69–0.99 for the legs, ‖Ĝ−I‖ = 3–71 for the hub-column correlations, so no alternating product converges to a trace state; and the layer-to-layer map is not an alternating product at all — the layer and gate algebras are nested (E_{l+1}E_l = E_{l+1}, rate 1), the forward map is multiplication by gate projections in the algebra, and the chain's step contains a single Mehler conditional expectation with Hermite-degree rate ρ^k, never iterated. The overlap operator that does exist is Cov(z_{l+1}, z_l) = T_{l+1←l}C_l + ½W D(w2)K3_21 (one-step cocycle on the covariance plus the κ3 slice feed; verified to ≤2e-3 with the κ3 term, 3–4% without), kink-weighted (ρφ_aφ_c) for the gate partitions, with small entries and O(10) norm from the collective mode. The one exact C3-type constant in the system is the Euler–Stein a = ∫½(1+τ)^{-3/2}ρ_τ^p dτ = 1/(p+1) with ρ_τ = (1+τ)^{-1/2} the Gaussian-pair maximal correlation along Eldan's path. The only new lead is minor: the Z leg TC_b is low-rank through the birth covariance (91/96/99% of P at k = 64/128/256), but it affects one of three n³ products per source-age and is 1e-2–1e-3 short of the required energy precision for young sources; a single kprop3c run with rank-256 C_b on ages ≥4 decides whether it is worth ~3–8% of the bill.
